decisions.name: §3 time versus space containments
decisions.reason: The deterministic time-space containments and configuration count are unrelated to the recursive-padding proof and are already developed on resource pages.
decisions.evidence: Read Vadhan Lecture 6 §3 in /tmp/step3a-sources.V7KhiK/vadhan-l6.txt: time bounds space, and configuration counting bounds deterministic time exponentially in space. Current recursive-padding page instead uses shortest accepting time, prefix simulation, quantitative self-reference and two downward inductions. These deterministic containment results are not required by that proof; the plan already has the space-complexity resource page.

decisions.name: Theorems 1-3 and nonidentity padding generalizations
decisions.reason: The current design explicitly selects the identity-padding specialization of Theorem 4; the broader speedup and padding results require additional interfaces and consumers.
decisions.evidence: Read the author-uploaded Seiferas–Fischer–Meyer article at the cited ResearchGate URL, printed pp147–148: Theorems 1–2 are diagonalization comparisons and Theorem 3 is Cook’s power separation. The current page explicitly selects identity padding; its lem-no-recursive-bound-covers-all-recursive-unary-languages supplies the required gross diagonal consequence locally. Declining the broader comparisons does not decline that needed local lemma or the owned Theorem-4 specialization.

decisions.name: §1 coNP, TAUT completeness, and NP versus coNP
decisions.reason: Complement classes and their open equality are not prerequisites for the SAT, 3SAT, or TQBF completeness proofs on this pair.
decisions.evidence: Read complete Kabanets l8 §1: TAUT/coNP completeness and the implication P=NP => NP=coNP. Current SAT page proves tableau satisfiability and a CNF clause-chain reduction; its quantified-space proof uses deterministic configuration reachability, not coNP closure or an equality assumption. The separate p-np-conp-and-polynomial-reductions page is in the plan.

decisions.name: §3 PCP theorem preview
decisions.reason: The lecture only previews probabilistically checkable proofs; PCP requires a later randomness and approximation development.
decisions.evidence: Read complete Kabanets l7 §3 (two-page lecture): the probabilistic constant-query verifier is explicitly a PCP preview, without its proof. The current tableau proof uses deterministic checking of an entire finite certificate and no random access verifier theorem. Adding PCP needs a new development outside these owned pages.

decisions.name: Theorem 3 NP is properly contained in NEXP
decisions.reason: That named class consequence belongs on the general hierarchy page; this pair supplies the stronger shifted-gap theorem it may later use.
decisions.evidence: Read complete Kabanets l10, including Theorem 3 proof NP subset NTIME(2^n) proper subset NTIME(2^(n^2)) subset NEXP. The current recursive-padding theorem supplies a separation stronger than this named consequence. Destination time-and-space-hierarchy-theorems exists in plan at order627 with thm-nondeterministic-time-hierarchy; this is a destination for later integration, not a claim that NP<NEXP is already an item or authorization to edit the published page.

decisions.name: §1 Theorem 1 Immerman-Szelepcsényi and inductive counting
decisions.reason: Closure of nondeterministic space under complement is separate space-complexity material and is not used by the deterministic PSPACE-hardness proof here.
decisions.evidence: Read complete Kabanets l12 §1 inductive-counting argument in /tmp/step3a-sources.V7KhiK/kabanets-l12.txt. The claimed result is NL=coNL and more generally nondeterministic-space complement closure. The proposed space-complexity-savitch-and-tqbf destination exists at order625, but its current item inventory supplies Savitch and deterministic PSPACE complement closure, not Immerman–Szelepcsényi. These are different claims. The current TQBF proof needs no inductive counting; owner must decide whether to add this separate result to the existing published destination.

decisions.name: §1 search-to-decision reductions
decisions.reason: Witness extraction under P equals NP neither supplies nor is used by recursive padding or the shortest-acceptance hierarchy argument.
decisions.evidence: Read complete Kabanets l10 §1: satisfying assignments are obtained by repeatedly fixing a variable and asking SAT under P=NP. Neither that hypothesis nor witness-extraction routine occurs on the current recursive-padding page; its quantitative self-reference and downward induction do not use search-to-decision.

decisions.name: §3 Theorem 4: NAE-SAT is NP-complete
decisions.reason: NAE-SAT is a different complete problem and no owned consumer needs its reduction or complement-symmetric assignments.
decisions.evidence: Read complete Kabanets l8 §3 Theorem4 proof, including the shared false variable and complement-symmetric assignments. This is a different target language from ordinary 3SAT. The current SAT inventory ends with ordinary clause-chain 3SAT and TQBF; no owned proof uses NAE clauses or complement symmetry.

decisions.name: Adjacent probabilistic and interactive-proof discussion
decisions.reason: Those models require randomness and interaction and belong to later complexity pages, not either completeness interface constructed here.
decisions.evidence: Current SAT/TQBF page and plan inventory were read: neither uses randomness or interactive protocols. However the declined source locator is only “Adjacent probabilistic and interactive-proof discussion”; the cached Arora SAT/space sections contain no matching discussion and do not establish which chapter/result was declined. Owner must identify the exact source section before this row can be upheld as a verified source disposition; no new content is licensed by this uncertainty.

decisions.name: §2 Theorem 2 Ladner's theorem
decisions.reason: Intermediate NP degrees under P not equal NP are unrelated to quantified reachability, and the current plan contains no page assigned to Ladner's theorem.
decisions.evidence: Read complete Kabanets l13 §2: Ladner’s conditional intermediate NP degrees are stated, not proved there. Current tableau and quantified-reachability constructions prove complete problems and assume no P-versus-NP separation. Plan has no assigned Ladner result in this pair. The decline preserves all current completeness claims.
